land.text: Gabès and Sfax: 'The region was only brought back under direct Hafsid control during the reign of Abu al-Abbas Ahmad II'

successors.note: The page gives Ahmad II's reign as 1371-1394 and the dynasty's years as 'from 1282 until 1394'.

capitals.name: Gabès
capitals.note: The page has the dynasty 'ruled over Gabès'; it names no other seat.

correction.text: Gabès, ruled by the Banu Makki 'from 1282'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page has no area. It says that 'at their height, sometime the early 14th century, their domain extended from Gabès to Tripoli' (with the nearby Jabal Nafusa), which the Banu Thabit page contradicts for Tripoli from c. 1324; the Gabès governorate is drawn alone.

correction.text: Gabès, Sfax and Tripoli, which the Genoese gave to the Banu Makki in 1354-1355

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'By the mid-1350s, they had extended their control to both Tripoli and Sfax' (Banu Makki page); 'the Genoese agreed to give the city to the Banu Makki, the rulers of Gabès' in 1354-1355 (Banu Thabit page).

correction.text: Gabès and Sfax, the 'effectively independent state' of the second half of the 14th century, after Tripoli was retaken in 1369-1370

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Bridging: the page names no change after the mid-1350s; the Hafsid sultan Ahmad II (1371-1394) brought the region back under direct control.

ledger.note: 1282: the Banu Makki rule Gabès. 'Banu Makki was a Muslim dynasty that ruled over Gabès from 1282 until 1394.' The family 'were able to get one of their own members to be appointed as governor in Gabès' (no year) under the Hafsids.

1354-55: the Genoese give Tripoli to the Banu Makki. 'The Genoese agreed to give the city to the Banu Makki, the rulers of Gabès, in exchange for a large payment' (1354-1355); the Banu Makki page: 'By the mid-1350s, they had extended their control to both Tripoli and Sfax.'
Mid-1350s: the Banu Makki extend their control to Sfax. 'By the mid-1350s, they had extended their control to both Tripoli and Sfax'; the page does not say from whom.
1369-70: Tripoli is retaken. Abu Bakr of the Banu Thabit 'retook the city in 1369-1370'.
1394: direct Hafsid control returns. 'The region was only brought back under direct Hafsid control during the reign of Abu al-Abbas Ahmad II (r. 1371-1394)'; the page's dynasty years end in 1394.
1394: the dynasty ends. 'Banu Makki was a Muslim dynasty that ruled over Gabès from 1282 until 1394.'

wars.name: Banu Thabit against the Banu Makki
wars.outcome: Abu Bakr of the Banu Thabit retook Tripoli in 1369-1370.

wars.name: Hafsid reassertion over Gabès
wars.outcome: The region 'was only brought back under direct Hafsid control during the reign of Abu al-Abbas Ahmad II (r. 1371-1394)'.
wars.note: The page names no battle and no year for the reconquest within the reign.

certainty.note: The page names Gabès, Sfax, Tripoli and the Jabal Nafusa with no frontier; the governorate and 25-40 km circles are the researcher's.

notes: Cliopatria has no Banu Makki row; its Hafsid Dynasty row carries Gabès and Tripolitania throughout. The Banu Makki page has no infobox and names no ruler except the Hafsid Ahmad II; its early-14th-century height 'from Gabès to Tripoli' (and the Jabal Nafusa) conflicts with the Banu Thabit page (Tripoli under the Banu Thabit from c. 1324) and is not drawn. The Hafsid dossier has no 1394 event for Gabès and records Tripoli's 1401 annexation under the counterpart 'nobody'. The page's 'an effectively independent state in the second half of the 14th century' has no year.

sources.title: Banu Makki
sources.note: Ruled Gabès 1282-1394, Tripoli and Sfax by the mid-1350s, Hafsid reassertion under Ahmad II.

sources.title: Banu Thabit
sources.note: The Genoese gave Tripoli to the Banu Makki in 1354-1355; Abu Bakr retook it in 1369-1370.
